fields.meta_title: Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Make a job application form that takes resumes and keeps every applicant in a table you own. Print a blank PDF for walk-ins. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline
fields.hero_description: Describe the role and what each applicant must provide. Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant table, and every answer stays in data you own.
fields.features_heading: What Every Job Application Form Needs
fields.features_subheading: A job application form asks every candidate for a role the same questions. These six pieces turn the answers into a shortlist.
fields.feature_1:
Every section, field by field

Emergent drafts the six standard sections with the right input for each answer: a date picker for the start date, a phone field, and a block that repeats for each past employer.
fields.feature_2:
One form for every open role

Applicants pick a position and see only the questions written for it. A nurse is asked for a license number and expiry date; a designer is asked for a portfolio and a salary range.
fields.feature_3:
Resume and certificate uploads

Applicants attach a resume and any license or certificate the role needs from a phone, without creating an account. Each file is stored with the application it arrived on.
fields.feature_4:
Blank and filled PDF copies

Print the blank form for walk-ins at the front counter. Each application that arrives online can also be kept as a filled PDF in the same layout, ready for the personnel file.
fields.feature_5:
An applicant table with hiring stages

Every application lands as a row with role, location, stage, and owner, in a table that never caps applications. The app then alerts the hiring manager by Slack or email.
fields.feature_6:
Your careers page, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it in the careers page you already run. Your developers get the full source in GitHub for anything the prompt did not cover.

fields.usecase_heading: Job Application Forms for Every Hire
fields.tab_content_1:
An hourly job application that leads with availability

The first question is which store. Applicants then give a start date and tap the shifts they can work. That store's manager hears about it in Slack, and a filter on the table shows at a glance who can cover weekends.
fields.tab_content_2:
A clinical job application that checks every credential

Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it, and medical assistants give their certification. Expiry dates get their own field, and anything due to lapse within 60 days is flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked. BLS and ACLS cards upload on the same screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
An internal application that loops in the manager

Employees apply with their employee ID and their months in the current role. This posting asks for at least 12, and anyone short of it is told before they submit. Eligible applications alert the person's current manager and go to a table kept apart from outside candidates.
fields.tab_content_4:
A professional application that sorts by must-haves

Designers and other salaried candidates upload a resume with a portfolio, then answer the must-have questions: work authorization and salary range. Missing either one sends the application to a hold list. Everyone else goes to the hiring manager as a Slack shortlist.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Job Application Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the usual sections, then add what each role needs. Seven steps take you from a list of requirements to a published form that fills an applicant table.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the role requires
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what you need to know before a first call: availability, location, licenses, the right to work, and pay expectations. A question that would not change the decision stays off the form. Applicants on a phone will finish a short form on a break; a long one waits for later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the sections you want, or ask for the standard set. Work history repeats for every past job the applicant lists, and references repeat the same way. The form closes with a certification the applicant signs and dates: I certify that my answers are true and complete.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each position its own questions in the prompt. A delivery role might ask about a driver's license and recent violations, while a cashier role skips them. Applicants see only the questions for the role they pick, and the shared sections read the same for everyone.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add an upload field for the resume and a second one for any certificate the role calls for, then mark which ones are required. A cover letter can stay optional for hourly roles and required for office ones.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who hears about each application and how: the store manager in Slack, the recruiter by email. Then name the stages every applicant moves through before an offer. With a stage column added, the applicant table becomes the hiring pipeline your managers filter each morning.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how paper applications get in. A QR code at the counter opens the same form on a phone, and a few blank printed copies cover anyone without one. When a paper copy comes back, a manager enters it through the online form and it joins the table.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on your careers page or your own domain, then submit a test application for every role. Check that each role shows its own questions and that the alert reaches the right person before the link goes out.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a job application form for the open roles at my company.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline', title 'Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent' and hero 'Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant database' cover the whole job, not one feature or a sibling topic (defect 1 clear).

intent.evidence: Cycle-1 fix holds: FAQ 3 lays out the form field by field ('Work history, per job: employer, title, dates, supervisor, reason for leaving, permission to contact'), howto_step_2 gives the certification text, and FAQ 8 and FAQ 11 cover the blank printable PDF the top 10 (rocklinusd, circuit7, Iowa, DS-1950 PDFs) serve. No AMBER angle needed (Builder-fit); F5 accepted.

specificity.evidence: Hiring variant in the table ('Prompt for the application form and the hiring pipeline around it'); buyer vocabulary throughout: 'reasons for leaving and permission to contact references', 'any license due to lapse within 60 days is flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked', 'months in the current role', 'a driver's license and recent violations' (defect 3 clear).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: feature_1 'Emergent drafts the six standard sections...', tab_content_1 'The first question is which store.', howto_step_6 'Decide what happens on paper.'; no keyword labels (defect 2 clear).

craft.evidence: Cycle-2 fix holds: zero ', so' and zero ', which' tails on the page; sentences end on their point ('...flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked.', 'Anything else waits for the interview.'); longest FAQ sentence well under 32 words; no 'and not before'-style trailers (defects 4, 6 clear).

voice.evidence: Cycle-2 fix holds: tab openings now differ in shape ('The first question is which store.' / 'Each nurse or medical assistant gives...' / 'Employees apply with...' / 'Designers and other salaried candidates upload...'); the role-example triplet is split (nurse/designer in feature_2, delivery/cashier in howto_step_3); 'six standard sections' appears once, 'one record, not an inbox' is gone; lines like 'Applicants on a phone will finish a short form on a break; a long one waits for later.' read human.

truth.evidence: PDF story is now one rule: FAQ 11 'The blank PDF has as many rows as you ask for: request one past job and one reference, and Emergent lays it out on a single letter page', consistent with FAQ 8 'blank PDF, sized for letter paper', FAQ 9 'the most recent job and one reference', FAQ 5 'printable version for walk-ins' and feature_4 'A PDF copy of any application'; 'instead of three' is gone; meta 'Print a PDF of any application' matches feature_4. FAQ 4, 13, 14 describe built-app behaviour ('the app can save...', 'the app can send a short decline') within the capability principle; the typed signature carries no legal-validity claim. Table facts from the library (V2/V3 clean); claims_used all approved.

distinct.evidence: Shift grid by store, clinical license-expiry flag, internal tenure check and must-have hold list are specific to hiring; new-employee-form, candidate-screening-form and creator-application are linked, not overlapped ('Payroll and emergency contact details come after the offer'); no sibling primary in a heading; D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 15 items, each answered in its first sentence ('Yes, if each section asks for less.', 'Usually not.'); cycle-2 repeats fixed with new information: FAQ 13 'set a size limit, for example 10 MB per file... refused at upload with a message', FAQ 14 'a confirmation email right away... a short decline', FAQ 4 'Haddad_RN.pdf'; FAQ 10 now answers use ('to decide whom to interview and hire'); FAQ 3 list is useful by design; links help ('new employee form', 'candidate screening form'); no contradictions between FAQ 4, 8, 9, 11.

images.evidence: Tab 1 'Maya Ortiz applied, Cashier, available weekends', 'Sent to Leo Park, store manager', 'Weekends: yes, start Nov 3' match the store/shift/weekend copy; tab 2 'Dana Ruiz... Expires in 52 days, under 60', 'Sent to Karen Bell, recruiter', 'BLS and ACLS on file', Ben Walsh renamed; tab 3 '18 months in role, minimum 12', 'Priya Shah, Customer Ops', 'Separate from outside hires'; tab 4 3 Shortlist + 1 On hold = 'Shortlist ready: 3 applicants' and 'Hold list 1'. One cursor per panel, text readable, no collisions, panels full (defects 5, 10 clear).

defects: why_description: Untrue generalization about competitors (catalogue rows 7 and 8): 'Form tools stop at the submit button.' Jotform, which is in this page's own table and top 10, sells Jotform Tables, Approvals and workflow routing after submit. -> Drop the claim about other tools and state what Emergent builds, e.g. 'Emergent builds the form, the applicant table and the manager alerts as one app, and the code is yours.' (stay within 25 words).

hero_description / features_subheading / why_description: The same sentence appears three times in three sections: 'Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant database' (hero), 'Emergent builds the form and the record it feeds' (features_subheading), 'Emergent builds the form and the applicant pipeline behind it as one app' (why). The sibling creator-application uses the same shape twice ('Emergent builds the form, scoring, review queue, and the database behind it', 'Emergent builds the form, the screening, and the creator roster as one build you own'), so this reads like a template with the nouns swapped (HUB_RULES 2b rhythm, rubric voice/distinct). 'the record it feeds' is also vague. -> Keep the hero sentence. Replace the second sentence of features_subheading with something only this section says, e.g. 'Below are the six sections Emergent drafts and what each application turns into once it is submitted.' Rewrite why_description without 'Emergent builds the form and...' (see the why_description fix above).

feature_1: 'Each field gets a proper input.' is vague filler that does not say what the reader gets (HUB_RULES 2a: 'Name the trigger, the field, the tool'). -> Name the inputs, e.g. 'Start dates get a date picker, phone numbers a phone field, and work history repeats for every past job.' Re-balance the body to 165-182 characters.

tab_content_1 / tab_image_1 / prompt_chip_2: The copy says 'Applicants then tap the shifts they can work on a weekly grid and give a start date', and the chip says 'Availability Grid'. The image has no grid: it shows three weekend chips (Sat AM, Sat PM, Sun PM), with the start date above them. The rubric's images test needs the copy and image to match word for word. -> Either redraw the main panel as a small weekly grid (days by AM/PM, with Sat AM, Sat PM and Sun PM selected) placed below the start date, or change the copy to 'Applicants give a start date, then tap the shifts they can work.' and rename chip 2 to match (e.g. 'Shift Availability').

tab_content_2 / tab_image_2: The copy says 'Each nurse or medical assistant gives a license number and the state that issued it', but the image's Grace Liu row reads 'CMA' with no state. That is also the truth: CMA is a national certification (AAMA), not a license a state issues, so the copy is wrong about medical assistants. -> Change the copy to 'Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it; medical assistants give their certification.' Alternatively, replace the CMA row with a state-licensed role (e.g. 'LPN, Kentucky') and limit the sentence to nurses.

tab_content_3 / tab_image_3: The copy says 'Anyone short of the posting's minimum tenure is told before they submit', but the image's timeline puts 'Tenure checked' after 'Application received 9:12 AM', which shows the check happening after submission. -> Reorder the steps to 'Tenure checked (18 months in role, minimum 12)' then 'Application submitted 9:12 AM' then 'Current manager alerted' then 'Hiring manager review'. Or relabel step 1 'Tenure confirmed before submit'.

tab_image_3 (mini card): The mini card reads 'Separate from outside hires', while the copy says 'a table kept apart from outside candidates'. 'Hires' means people already hired, not external applicants, so the label is wrong. -> Change the mini card sub to 'Separate from outside candidates'.

tab_image_4: The story is that the list is 'Sorted by must-haves' (work authorization and salary range), and the hero says 'Each one meets every must-have'. Yet the shortlisted rows show unrelated or partial facts: Mara Cole 'Remote, portfolio attached' (a portfolio is not a must-have), Tom Baker 'Office, salary in range' (no authorization), Lena Fox 'Remote, work authorization' (no salary). The panel does not show why these three passed. -> Make every shortlisted sub show both must-haves, e.g. 'Remote, authorized, salary in range'. Keep Ivan Petrov 'No work authorization' as the one on hold.

feature_5 / why_table: One thing has three names on the page: 'applications' (body), 'a table that never caps submissions' (feature_5) and 'Response limits' / 'Where responses live' (table rows). HUB_RULES 2a says to use the same term for the same thing. -> feature_5: 'in a table that never caps applications'. Regenerate the table with row labels 'limits=Application limits' and 'data=Where applications live' (the same label override as 'uploads=Resume uploads').

faq item 4 (Can I download a job application form PDF?): The top 10 are blank PDFs and DOCs (rocklinusd, circuit7, Iowa, DS-1950), so this question asks for a blank form. The answer says 'Yes.' and then describes only filled copies of submitted applications, which misleads the searcher. The blank PDF only shows up four items later, in FAQ 8. -> Answer the blank form first: 'Yes. The form Emergent builds can give you a blank PDF of the same questions to print, and it can save each submitted application as a filled PDF ending with the applicant's typed signature and date.' Keep the Haddad_RN.pdf naming line. Trim FAQ 8 to the free-to-start and paper-intake points so the two don't repeat.

faq item 12 (Do I need separate job application forms for each role?): The question is about roles, but the evidence is about locations: 'Separate copies per location tend to drift: one store rewrites its availability question and the others never hear about it.' The answer then concludes about roles ('one form that branches by position'). The middle sentence argues a different question. -> Make the example about roles, e.g. 'Separate copies per role tend to drift: the cashier form gets a new availability question and the stock-clerk form never does.'
